elevator-apparent-weight.alt: A 70 kg rider on a scale in an elevator, three times, with g = 9.8 m/s². Accelerating up at 1.2 m/s²: F_N, scale on rider, is longer than F_g, Earth on rider, and the scale reads 770 N. Constant velocity: equal arrows, 686 N. Accelerating down at 1.2 m/s²: F_N is shorter than F_g, 602 N. The gravitational force, 686 N, is the same in all three.

gravitation-two-spheres.alt: Two spheres of masses m1 and m2 a distance r apart, center to center, pull each other with equal and opposite forces along the line joining their centers. A panel gives |F_g| = Gm1m2/r² and how it scales: doubling r divides F by 4, tripling r divides it by 9, doubling m1 doubles it, doubling both masses multiplies it by 4.
